questions.question: For a system of $m$ independent linear equations in $n$ variables, which description fits the nonbasic variables of a basic solution?
options: The variables that turn out to be zero after solving the system
The $m$ variables whose values are solved from the equations
The $n-m$ variables chosen outside the basis and set to zero
The slack variables added to turn inequalities into equations

questions.question: A basic solution of an augmented LP has been computed, and the slack variable $s_2$ has value $0$ in it. What can be concluded from this value alone?
options: $s_2$ is nonbasic, because only nonbasic variables are zero
Nothing yet: a basic variable can also have value zero
$s_2$ is basic, because slack variables always stay basic
The basic solution is infeasible, since slacks must be positive

questions.question: When a basic solution is formed from $m$ independent linear equations in $n$ variables, why are exactly $n-m$ variables set to zero?
options: Then $m$ equations remain for $m$ unknowns, solvable uniquely
Then all $n$ values are guaranteed to be nonnegative
These $n-m$ variables have zero objective coefficients
Then the $n$ values give the largest possible objective value

questions.question: An LP constraint $\sum_j a_{ij}x_j\le b_i$ is written as $\sum_j a_{ij}x_j+s_i=b_i$ with slack $s_i\ge0$. At a basic solution, $s_i$ is nonbasic. What does this say about constraint $i$ at that solution?
options: It is dropped from the model at this solution
It holds with equality: all of $b_i$ is used
None of the resource $b_i$ is used at all
It is violated, since its slack is not basic

questions.question: An LP $\max\ c_1x_1+c_2x_2$ subject to $\le$ constraints with nonnegative right-hand sides is put in augmented form with one slack per constraint. In the usual initial basic solution with the slacks as basis, which variables are nonbasic?
options: $x_1$ and $x_2$, each fixed at the value zero
All slack variables, each equal to zero
No variables, since all variables are basic initially
$x_1$ and $x_2$, equal to their upper bounds

questions.question: An LP has $4$ decision variables and $3$ functional $\le$ constraints. Each constraint gets its own slack variable, giving $3$ independent equations. How many variables are nonbasic in each basic solution?
The LP constraints $x_1+x_2\le6$, $x_1+2x_2\le8$ and $x_1\le5$ get slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3$. Which point $(x_1,x_2)$ is the basic solution with nonbasic variables $x_1$ and $s_2$?

The augmented system $2x_1+x_2+s_1=10$, $x_1+2x_2+s_2=11$, $x_2+s_3=5$ has the basic solution $(x_1,x_2,s_1,s_2,s_3)=(5,0,0,6,5)$, in which exactly two variables are zero. Which variables are nonbasic?
options: $x_2$ only
$s_1$ only

questions.question: At a basic solution of an equality system, one nonbasic variable is raised from $0$ while all other nonbasic variables stay at $0$. What happens to the basic variables?
options: They change so that all equations remain satisfied
They keep their values, since only nonbasic variables move
They all fall to zero and become nonbasic in turn
They rise by the same amount as the raised variable

questions.question: At a basic solution with $m$ independent equations in $n$ variables, one nonbasic variable is made basic. What must happen for the result to be a basic solution again?
options: No variable leaves; the basis simply grows
Exactly one basic variable becomes nonbasic
Every other nonbasic variable becomes basic
Two basic variables become nonbasic

questions.question: The system $x_1+x_2+s_1=6$, $x_1+2x_2+s_2=8$, $x_1+s_3=5$ has the basic solution with $s_1,s_2$ nonbasic: $x_1=4$, $x_2=2$, $s_3=1$. Now $s_2$ is raised from $0$ to $1$ while $s_1=0$. By how much does $x_2$ change?
options: It increases by $1$
It decreases by $\frac{1}{2}$
It does not change
It decreases by $1$

questions.question: The system $x_1+x_2+s_1=6$, $x_1+2x_2+s_2=8$, $x_1+s_3=4$ (all variables nonnegative) has the basic solution with $s_1,s_2$ nonbasic: $(x_1,x_2,s_1,s_2,s_3)=(4,2,0,0,0)$. Which variables are basic although their value is $0$?
options: $s_1$ and $s_2$, fixed at zero by choice
$s_1$, $s_2$ and $s_3$, as all three slacks are zero
No zero-valued variable is basic here
Only $s_3$, solved from the third equation

questions.question: The LP constraints $2x_1+x_2\le10$, $x_1+2x_2\le11$ and $x_2\le5$ are written as equations with slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3\ge0$. Fixing $s_1=s_3=0$ as nonbasic, what are the basic values, and is this basic solution feasible?

In an LP with $\le$ constraints and slack variables, the decision variable $x_1$ is nonbasic at the initial basic solution with the slacks as basis. What does this imply about $x_1$ in other basic solutions?
options: Nothing: another basis can make $x_1$ basic and positive
$x_1$ stays nonbasic, since only slacks can leave the basis
$x_1$ is zero in every feasible solution of the LP
$x_1$ can become basic, but its value then stays zero

questions.question: An LP has $p$ decision variables and $m$ functional $\le$ constraints, each with its own slack. At some basic solution exactly $k$ of the decision variables are basic. How many slack variables are nonbasic at this solution?
options: $p-k$
$m-k$

questions.question: The LP constraints $2x_1+x_2\le10$, $x_1+2x_2\le11$, $x_2\le5$ get slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3$, giving three equations in five variables. Which pair of variables can NOT be the nonbasic pair of any basic solution?
The LP constraints $x_1+x_2\le5$, $x_1\le3$, $x_2\le2$ get slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3$. How many different choices of two nonbasic variables give a basic solution located at the point $(x_1,x_2)=(3,2)$?
